<result>I have a complete, confirmed picture. Here's my report.

## Summary

The i18n machinery is fully built and already runs over the API + CSS trees — but only with the **deterministic `glossary` adapter**, which swaps a fixed list of TypeDoc structural terms and leaves all actual prose in English. Adding "API typedoc / cssdoc prose" to translation is really about routing that tree through the **`claude-code` adapter** (real prose translation, like the guides already get) without the cold-cache cost the maintainers explicitly warned against.

---

## 1. Docs site structure

- **Site root:** `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/docs` — a VitePress site, package `@pantoken/docs` (`docs/package.json`).
- **VitePress config dir:** `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/docs/.vitepress/`
  - `config.ts` (20 KB) — main config. Reads `LOCALES` from `i18n.ts`, builds `localesConfig` per locale, loads per-locale TypeDoc sidebars via `typedocSidebarByLocale` (line 71), and splits the API sidebar with `splitApiSidebar` (line 169). Live CSS `@example` previews are seamed in via `demoMarkdownIt` from `@pantoken/demo` (imported line 5).
  - **`i18n.ts`** (the translation/UI layer) — `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/docs/.vitepress/i18n.ts`. Defines `DocsLocale = "root" | "hu"` and `LOCALES`, holding every localizable UI string: nav/sidebar labels, `editText`, `themeSelector`, VitePress chrome, and local-search UI. Note `typedocSidebarPath` differs per locale (`../api/...` vs `../hu/api/...`).
- **Locales:** two — `root` (English, `/…`) and `hu` (Magyar/Hungarian, `/hu/…`). Symmetric prefix swap using VitePress default routing (no custom `i18nRouting`).
- **Content trees:** `docs/guide/` (hand-written EN guides), `docs/hu/guide/` (translated), `docs/api/` (generated EN API + CSS), `docs/hu/api/` (cloned + adapter-processed).

## 2. The i18n translation workflow

Scripts live in `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/docs/scripts/`:

- **`api-translation.ts`** — the adapter architecture. Interface `TranslationAdapter` (`translateMarkdown` / `translateText` / optional `translateBatch`). Two implementations:
  - `GlossaryTranslationAdapter` (`name = "glossary"`, the CI-safe default) — applies `SORTED_REPLACEMENTS`, a fixed ~55-term glossary of TypeDoc structural words (Parameters→Paraméterek, Returns→Visszatérés, etc.). Preserves fenced/inline code and `@scope/pkg` names. **Does not translate prose.**
  - `ClaudeCodeTranslationAdapter` (`name = "claude-code"`) — shells out to `claude -p`, real translation, with code/package placeholder protection and JSON batch mode.
  - `createTranslationAdapter()` picks via `DOCS_TRANSLATION_ADAPTER` env (default `glossary`).
- **`translation-memory.ts`** — content-addressed cache (`TranslationMemory`, `keyFor` = sha256 of kind+source, `translateUnits`). Committed cache dir `docs/i18n-cache/` (`hu.guides.json`, `hu.api.json`). Only new/edited units reach the adapter; markdown translated per-file, short labels batched.
- **`build-api-locales.ts`** — regenerates EN API (TypeDoc → `style-api-badges.ts` → `write-api-overview.ts`), builds CSS API, **clones `docs/api` → `docs/hu/api`**, then runs the adapter over every `.md` and every `typedoc-sidebar.json` label. This is where the API/CSS prose translation would plug in.
- **`translate-guides.ts`** — translates `docs/guide/*.md` → `docs/<locale>/guide/`. Same adapter selector. This is a **manual, committed** workflow.
- **`check-locale-parity.ts`** — asserts HU guide + API trees mirror root page-for-page.

**Relevant package.json scripts** (`docs/package.json`):
- `docs:api:locales` → glossary (default); `docs:api:locales:claude` → `DOCS_TRANSLATION_ADAPTER=claude-code`
- `docs:guides:locales` → glossary; `docs:guides:locales:claude` → claude-code
- `docs:check:locales`, `docs:build`, `docs:build:claude`
- Root `package.json` proxies: `docs:dev`, `docs:build`, `docs:api`.

## 3. Guides vs API/cssdoc prose — what's actually translated

This is the crux. **Both trees run through the same pipeline, but with different adapters in practice:**

- **Guides** — the committed `docs/hu/guide/*.md` are **real Hungarian prose** (verified: `docs/hu/guide/packages.md` opens "# A csomagtérkép / A pantoken egy monorepo…"). Produced by the **claude-code** adapter. `hu.guides.json` holds 7 full-page translations.
- **API (TypeDoc) + CSS (cssdoc) prose** — committed `docs/hu/api/**` is **glossary output only**. Verified against `docs/hu/api/css/button.md` vs `docs/api/css/button.md`: only structural labels changed (`Source`→`Forrás`, `Examples`→`Példák`, `Description`→`Leírás`). The actual prose is still English — component description, the Accessibility paragraph, modifier descriptions ("An AI action.", "A destructive action."), and even section headings `Accessibility` / `Usage` / `Demo` / `Modifiers` (these cssdoc headings aren't in the glossary at all — confirmed no match in `api-translation.ts`).
- `hu.api.json` has ~1,130 entries, but they're glossary-processed markdown/labels (mostly-English bodies), not real translations.

**Why:** `docs/conventions/build-and-docs.md` "Adapter split" — "Hand-written guides use the `claude-code` adapter; the generated API tree (TypeDoc + CSS reference) uses the deterministic `glossary` adapter. Don't run `:claude` over the whole API tree — a cold cache means hundreds of sequential `claude -p` calls."

So the scoping gap is deliberate: nobody wanted hundreds of sequential Claude calls in the build. The pipeline already *supports* claude-code for the API tree (`docs:api:locales:claude` exists); it's just not used because of cost/latency, and the incremental memory only helps after the first expensive full run.

## 4. Where API/cssdoc content comes from

- **TypeDoc config:** `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/docs/typedoc.json` (+ `tsconfig.typedoc.json`). Plugins: `typedoc-plugin-markdown`, `typedoc-vitepress-theme`, and local `../plugins/typedoc/demo/dist/index.mjs`. ~24 entry points across `packages/`, `formats/`, `platforms/`, `renderers/`, `bundlers/`, `design/`, `ai/`, `plugins/`, `tools/`. Prose comes from TSDoc comments in source. Output → `docs/api/`, sidebar → `docs/api/typedoc-sidebar.json`.
- **CSS API (cssdoc):** `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/docs/scripts/build-css-api.ts`. A thin wrapper: builds pantoken's `resolveToken`/`resolveSource`/`importSnippet` hooks, then calls `@cssdoc/typedoc`'s `emitCssApi`, which writes `docs/api/css/**` and merges a "CSS" section into the TypeDoc sidebar. Prose comes from `@component`/`@utility`/`@rule`/`@declaration` doc comments in `formats/components/**` CSS/TS sources, parsed by `@cssdoc/core`. Rendering lives in `@cssdoc/markdown` (consumed from npm, not workspace). Config: `/Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken/cssdoc.jsonc` (section order, `headingPrefix: "CSS:"`). Live `<div class="css-example">` previews are pantoken's `@pantoken/typedoc-plugin-live-example`, seamed at compile time by `demoMarkdownIt`, not baked into the `.md`.
- **Post-processing:** `style-api-badges.ts` + `api-badge-classes.ts` (badge classes, kept in sync with cssdoc deprecation markers), `write-api-overview.ts` (API landing blurb).
- Both TypeDoc and CSS pages land under `docs/api/` (then cloned to `docs/hu/api/`), so they share one sidebar and nav — the CSS section rides inside `typedoc-sidebar.json`.

## What is vs isn't translated (bottom line)

| Content | Adapter used | Prose translated? |
|---|---|---|
| VitePress UI chrome, nav, sidebar labels | `i18n.ts` `LOCALES` (hand-authored) | Yes |
| Hand-written guides (`docs/hu/guide/`) | `claude-code` | Yes (real Hungarian) |
| TypeDoc API prose (`docs/hu/api/**`) | `glossary` | No — structural terms only |
| cssdoc prose (`docs/hu/api/css/**`) | `glossary` | No — and cssdoc section headings (Accessibility/Usage/Demo/Modifiers) aren't even in the glossary |

## Key files for the work

- `docs/scripts/build-api-locales.ts` — the integration point; already calls `translateUnits` over the whole cloned tree.
- `docs/scripts/api-translation.ts` — where an improved API-prose strategy (e.g. a hybrid glossary+claude adapter, or extending the glossary with cssdoc section headings) would live.
- `docs/scripts/translation-memory.ts` — the incremental cache that makes a one-time full claude run affordable on re-runs (`autosave` already supports resumable long runs).

# Build, release, and the docs site

## Use the `vp` toolchain, never pnpm directly

- `vp` / `vpr` / `vpx` are **global** bins. Run tasks via `vp run <task>`, execute bins via `vp exec
[-F <glob>] <bin>`.
- **Package scripts must never shell out to `pnpm`.** CI (`.github/workflows/docs.yml`) provides `vp`
  via `voidzero-dev/setup-vp` but **not** `pnpm` on PATH, so a `pnpm run …` inside any script breaks
  the docs deploy with `pnpm: command not found`. Local dev has pnpm, so a top-level `pnpm run X` is
  fine — but scripts it calls must stay pnpm-free internally.
- `.css` formatting: `vp fmt` (oxc) is JS/TS/JSON only and no-ops on `.css`. Stylelint owns `.css` —
  `lint:css` runs `stylelint --fix`, wired into `ready` and the `vite.config.ts` `staged` hook.

## The gate

- `pnpm run ready` — build `-r`, `vp check`, test `-r`, markdown lint. Must pass before you're done.
- `pnpm run check:publish` — `publint`.
- Release automation uses Changesets and package-tag workflows in
  `.github/workflows/release.yml`.
- Use `pnpm run release:version` to apply package changelog/version updates, then
  `vp run release:changelog:root` to rebuild the strict chronological root `CHANGELOG.md` before
  creating package tags.
- Generated artifacts are gitignored and reproduced on build: `platforms/tokens/src/generated/`,
  `platforms/css/style.css`, each preprocessor's static file, and web-components `src/generated/`.
  `ready` runs `vp run -r build` before `vp check`, so generated files exist in order.

See `docs/internal/release-strategy.md` for the runbook, dist-tag mapping, prerelease flow, and npm
organization governance model.

## Linting CSS

Root `stylelint.config.js` runs error-only core rules plus `@cssdoc/stylelint-plugin`'s
`cssdoc/valid-doc-comments`; anchor-positioning props are ignored and `@scope` is allowed. A parallel
`eslint.config.js` runs `@cssdoc/eslint-plugin` (via `@eslint/css`) over the same `.css` (`lint:js`).
`lint:css` targets the web-components `src/**/*.css` sources and the generated components CSS.

## The docs site

`docs/` is a VitePress site (`@pantoken/docs`) with two locales — `root` (English, `/…`) and `hu`
(Magyar, `/hu/…`) — a symmetric prefix swap that VitePress's default routing already handles (don't
set a custom `i18nRouting`).

- **Translation layer is `docs/.vitepress/i18n.ts`.** `LOCALES[locale]` holds every localizable UI
  string (nav/sidebar labels, `editText`, the theme selector, VitePress chrome labels, and local
  search). `config.ts` expands these into per-locale `themeConfig` (search is the exception — it lives
  in the global `themeConfig.search.options.locales`). Add new UI strings here, never inline.
- **Adapter split.** Hand-written guides use the `claude-code` adapter; the generated API tree
  (TypeDoc + CSS reference) uses the deterministic `glossary` adapter. Don't run `:claude` over the
  whole API tree — a cold cache means hundreds of sequential `claude -p` calls.

## The cssdoc integration

pantoken consumes `@cssdoc/*` from **npm** (catalog entries; consumers use `catalog:`), not a local
workspace link. `docs/scripts/build-css-api.ts` is a thin wrapper: it builds pantoken's `resolveToken`
(syntax + value + local vars) and `resolveDemo` hooks, then calls `@cssdoc/typedoc`'s `emitCssApi`,
and keeps the `unknownReferences` drift guard. All page/index/sidebar rendering lives in
`@cssdoc/markdown`. The live `<div class="css-example">` preview is pantoken's own
`@pantoken/typedoc-plugin-live-example`, kept out of `@cssdoc/markdown` so the upstream stays generic.

**Catalog gotcha:** cssdoc packages reference `catalog:` deps; if cssdoc adds a new one, pantoken's
catalog must carry it too, or install fails with `ERR_PNPM_CATALOG_ENTRY_NOT_FOUND_FOR_SPEC`.

## The nested-`vp`-spawn limitation

Under `vpr docs:dev`, VitePress runs _under_ `vp`. Any `vp run …` / `vp pack` spawned from **inside**
that process dies with `Failed to spawn process: Invalid argument (os error 22)` on a cache miss. A
direct `node scripts/x.ts` is unaffected. So:

- The docs orchestrator's `upstream[].build` uses `["node","scripts/generate.ts"]` (cwd = the package
  dir), not a nested `vp run`.
- The CSS-API node runs `["node","scripts/build-css-api.ts"]` (cwd `docs`).
- `@pantoken/web-components`' `register()` bundle genuinely needs `vp pack` (which also can't nest), so
  it's not in the live orchestrator — rebuild it in a separate top-level shell
  (`vpr @pantoken/web-components#build`); `reloadWatchPaths` on its `dist` bridges the change into HMR.

A `vp run X && vp run Y` chain _inside_ a package.json script is fine — that's a top-level
script-runner context, not a spawn from within the running VitePress process.

content.thinking:
I'm getting clarity on the core issue: the current pipeline runs the Claude adapter over the entire API tree, which causes hundreds of sequential API calls with a cold cache. The maintainers want to scope this more carefully—likely targeting only the specific prose sections that need localization rather than processing everything at once. e the cold-cache risk — if we commit the translation cache upfront, subsequent updates only need incremental runs. Option C trades one expensive initial pass for long-term affordability and maintainability. So guides are a purely manual committed artifact—they're only regenerated when someone explicitly runs the script, and the committed Hungarian guide files are what the build actually uses. The API tree works differently: `docs:build` regenerates it from scratch every time by running the glossary adapter, so it's rebuilt on each build rather than being a static committed artifact.

The real constraint is that if we want prose translations for the API tree, we can't just commit the translated files since the build regenerates them anyway. The build itself needs to produce the translations, which means either running the expensive claude-code translation during CI (not feasible on a cold cache), or storing the claude-translated prose in the committed translation memory file keyed by content hash, then serving it from cache during the build.

The key realization is that `translateUnits` checks the translation memory first regardless of which adapter is configured—the cache key is adapter-independent, based on content hash. So if we populate `hu.api.json` with claude translations once, a subsequent glossary build would still hit that cache for the same content and serve the claude translations, only falling back to the glossary adapter for new or edited files.

This creates an elegant solution: the committed translation memory carries the high-quality claude prose, while CI runs the glossary adapter (which mostly cache-hits, staying cold-cache-safe and avoiding claude calls), yet still ships the real translations.

But there's a catch with file-level content addressing — any change to the markdown invalidates the entire file's cache entry, forcing a fallback to glossary. Since TypeDoc output shifts with every signature tweak, file-level cache hits become rare in practice, leaving most files stuck with English prose. That's why the current design keeps API on glossary: the granularity is too coarse for volatile generated docs. To make prose translation stick, I need finer-grained translation units instead of whole-file caching.

The real fix is block-level translation. I'd split each markdown file into segments, classify them as prose or scaffolding, hash and cache prose blocks individually, then translate only those blocks through Claude while keeping structural labels on glossary. This way signature changes don't invalidate the prose cache, and I'm making far fewer, smaller translation calls.

For TypeDoc, the prose lives in description paragraphs, remarks, parameter descriptions, and example captions. For cssdoc, it's component descriptions, accessibility and usage sections, and modifier descriptions. The tricky part is figuring out how to segment the markdown intelligently.

I could split on blank lines and classify each block as either translatable prose or something to preserve like code fences and tables. Or I could use a markdown parser to tokenize and only translate paragraph and text tokens. The classification is where things get fragile, but it's the right level of granularity.

Actually, I should step back and think about what the user really needs here. They asked for a plan with tradeoffs, so I should identify the key decisions they need to make upfront rather than diving into implementation details.

There are a few forks to work through. First, granularity: do I translate the whole file at once (simpler but cache-thrashes on generated docs) or extract prose at the block level (more durable cache but more code)? Second, where does the expensive translation run happen — should it be a manual local run that gets committed to cache like the guides, with CI just serving the cached version? That seems like the established pattern already. Third, there's a gap with the cssdoc section headings that aren't in the glossary yet. Those need to be handled either by adding them to the glossary upfront (deterministic and safe since they're a fixed set from cssdoc.jsonc) or some other way.

The real question is whether whole-file translation is viable given cache invalidation. If TypeDoc regenerates deterministically when the source doesn't change, then the content hash stays the same and the cache hits — invalidation only happens when the actual source changes, not on every build.

But there's a problem: doc comments, line numbers in "Defined in" links, and resolved token values all shift when unrelated code changes. So a single edit to one component's doc comment causes that entire page's cache to miss, reverting all its prose back to English until the next Claude run. Worse, a refactor touching line numbers across many files triggers mass cache misses and mass English fallback, which degrades the translated docs site between runs and leaves CI unable to recover it.

Block-level caching would be more resilient—editing one doc comment only misses that prose block's cache, leaving the rest of the page translated. The "Defined in" line-number churn wouldn't even touch the prose blocks since they're separate segments. It's more durable, though it requires more work and fragile classification logic. That's the honest tradeoff to present.

Actually, there might be a cleaner path: translate at the cssdoc or TSDoc segment level by hooking the renderers directly. But those libraries are external npm packages, so hooking them isn't straightforward.

The pragmatic approach is post-processing the rendered markdown—that's where the pipeline already works. So the recommendation is block-level segmentation with post-processing.

Now I need to sketch out the concrete implementation: a new segmentation module that splits rendered markdown into an ordered list of segments.

Building the segmentation logic... For each prose segment I'll cache the key and translate only what's missing, then reassemble everything. I should also extend the glossary to cover cssdoc section headings like Accessibility and Usage — that's a quick win that doesn't depend on the prose work. The scripts stay the same: the manual claude run populates the cache locally, then CI's glossary build uses that cache and falls back for any gaps. I need to update the docs to explain how the adapter split works.

Now I'm verifying the core assumption: the cache key is based on kind and source only, not the adapter or locale, so a glossary build will serve whatever claude translations are committed in the cache file regardless of what generated them. But there's a catch in the save logic — it prunes to only the keys used in that run, so if CI runs glossary and a PR changes what gets used, the cache could lose entries. If a prose block gets deleted from the docs, the cache entry gets pruned on the next save, which is the right behavior. The main risk is that moving from file-level markdown entries to block-level prose entries changes the cache key structure entirely, so the existing 1,130 glossary entries become orphaned and get pruned — but that's acceptable since the full tree is always processed in a single build run.

The first block-level run will hit a cold cache and need a Claude pass to populate the prose blocks, which is a one-time cost I can live with. I'm thinking I should launch a Plan agent to pressure-test the block-level segmentation approach and surface any edge cases, since the workflow recommends it and this is genuinely a non-trivial design decision.

Actually, I'm reconsidering whether I need to ask the user questions upfront. Block-level is clearly superior for durability and CI safety compared to whole-file caching, but there's a real scope fork here—block-level requires segmentation and classification work, while a simpler whole-file approach is much cheaper but has degradation tradeoffs. That's a legitimate decision the user should weigh. I also need to clarify whether they're just scoping this now or looking to ship it.

Let me spin up a Plan agent to validate the approach, then ask about granularity and scope before writing out the full plan.

I'm scoping how to add real prose translation to the generated API docs (TypeDoc + cssdoc) in the pantoken monorepo at /Users/dwahl/Scripts/pantoken. I need you to pressure-test a design and surface edge cases. This is planning only — do NOT edit anything.

## Context (already confirmed by exploration)

The docs site (`docs/`, VitePress, locales `root`=EN and `hu`=Hungarian) has an i18n pipeline:

- `docs/scripts/build-api-locales.ts` regenerates EN API (TypeDoc + cssdoc via `build-css-api.ts`), then clones `docs/api` → `docs/hu/api` and runs a translation adapter over every `.md` file (per whole file, kind `"markdown"`) and every `typedoc-sidebar.json` label (kind `"text"`, batched).
- `docs/scripts/api-translation.ts` has two adapters: `GlossaryTranslationAdapter` (deterministic, ~55 fixed structural-term replacements like Parameters→Paraméterek; preserves code fences + `@scope/pkg`; does NOT translate prose) and `ClaudeCodeTranslationAdapter` (shells out to `claude -p`, real prose translation, with code/package placeholder protection + JSON batch mode). Selected via `DOCS_TRANSLATION_ADAPTER` env, default `glossary`.
- `docs/scripts/translation-memory.ts` is a content-addressed cache: key = `sha256(kind + " " + source)` — ADAPTER-AGNOSTIC and committed as `docs/i18n-cache/hu.api.json`. `translateUnits` serves cache hits first; only misses reach the adapter. `save()` prunes to keys used this run. `autosave` makes long runs resumable.
- Scripts: `docs:api:locales` (glossary, used by CI `docs:build`), `docs:api:locales:claude` (claude-code). Guides use the same machinery and are real Hungarian — someone ran claude once and committed `docs/hu/guide/*.md` + `hu.guides.json`.
- CONSTRAINT (from `docs/conventions/build-and-docs.md`): "Don't run `:claude` over the whole API tree — a cold cache means hundreds of sequential `claude -p` calls." CI provides `vp` but not `pnpm`; scripts must not shell out to pnpm.
- GAP: cssdoc section headings (Accessibility, Usage, Demo, Modifiers, from `cssdoc.jsonc` sectionOrder) aren't in the glossary, so they render in English even under glossary.

## The design I want you to validate

The whole `.md` file is the wrong translation-unit granularity for GENERATED docs: TypeDoc output changes on any signature edit, "Defined in" line-number shift, or token-value change, so whole-file content hashes thrash → cache misses → the whole page's prose reverts to English (glossary) until claude is re-run. CI (glossary) can't recover it.

Proposed: **block-level prose segmentation**. Split each rendered `.md` into ordered segments, classify each as `prose` (translatable) vs `preserve` (verbatim: frontmatter, fenced code, HTML blocks like badges and `<div class="css-example">`, type/signature tables, structural-label headings, links/anchors). Hash and cache only prose segments individually. Translate prose via claude, glossary-map structural headings, reassemble. This keeps the cache warm across scaffolding churn and bounds the cold-run cost to distinct doc-comment paragraphs.

Workflow model: run `docs:api:locales:claude` locally once (populates prose segments into committed `hu.api.json`); CI's glossary build serves those prose translations from the adapter-agnostic cache and only falls back to glossary for genuinely-new prose. Also extend the glossary with the fixed cssdoc section headings.

## What I need from you

1. Is the "adapter-agnostic committed cache serves claude prose to a glossary CI build" model actually sound given `translateUnits` + `save()` pruning semantics? Any way it silently drops or corrupts the committed claude prose on a glossary run?
2. Pressure-test the block-level segmentation: what are the hard classification cases in TypeDoc-markdown + cssdoc output? Look at real rendered files — read `docs/api/css/button.md` and a couple of TypeDoc `.md` files under `docs/api/` (e.g. a function or interface page) to see actual structure. Where's the prose vs scaffolding boundary? How should param/property table descriptions (prose inside tables) be handled — translate or defer to v1?
3. Concrete integration: what should change in `build-api-locales.ts` (per-file → per-segment loop), what new module(s), what new unit `kind`, and does `translation-memory.ts` need changes?
4. Cache migration: moving whole-file `markdown` keys → per-block `prose` keys invalidates the existing committed `hu.api.json`. Confirm the first block-level run must be a claude run, and that this is acceptable/bounded.
5. Any simpler viable alternative I'm missing, and its tradeoff vs block-level.

Read the four scripts named above and the rendered example files. Return a concrete, critical assessment with specific file/line references and a recommended segmentation boundary.

3	`.instui-button` — An accessible action control, styled from the token palette; primary by default.

5	The AI variants layer two gradients — a padding-box fill and a border-box stroke — for their frame, and `-color-ai-secondary` can't paint gradient text and a fill at once, so its centre stays transparent at rest and fills on hover or active. # CSS: button

`.instui-button` — An accessible action control, styled from the token palette; primary by default.

The AI variants layer two gradients — a padding-box fill and a border-box stroke — for their frame, and `-color-ai-secondary` can't paint gradient text and a fill at once, so its centre stays transparent at rest and fills on hover or active. Ghost hover and active derive a low-opacity, slightly-darkened brand wash rather than using the raw hover-background tokens, which would print same-colour-on-same-colour text.

**Source:** [button.ts](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/blob/main/formats/components/src/components/button.ts)

## Accessibility

Drive the `-toggle` variant's pressed state with `aria-pressed`, and mark a disabled button with `aria-disabled` (or the native `disabled`).

## Usage

```css
@import "@pantoken/components/components.css";
@import "@pantoken/components/button.css";
```

## Demo

```demo
self:button
```

## Examples

```html
<button class="instui-button">Primary</button>
```

## Modifiers

| Modifier | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `.-color-ai` | An AI action. |
| `.-color-ai-secondary` | A lower-emphasis AI action. |
| `.-color-danger` | A destructive action. |
| `.-color-primary-inverse` | Primary action for dark backgrounds. |
| `.-color-secondary` | A lower-emphasis secondary action. |
| `.-color-success` | A positive/confirming action. |
| `.-color-tertiary` | A text-style action (no fill or border until hover). |
| `.-condensed` | Tighter padding for dense toolbars. |
| `.-display-block` | Full-width block button. |
| `.-ghost` | Outline (ghost) style: a border in the colour's ghost tokens, no fill. |
| `.-icon-*` | Render a glyph from the icon set before the label (e.g. `-icon-arrow-right`), painted in the button's text colour; pair with `-shape-square`/`-shape-circle` for an icon-only button. |
| `.-shape-circle` | A round icon button. |
| `.-shape-square` | A square icon button. |
| `.-size-large` | Large. Long-form alias of `-size-lg`. |
| `.-size-lg` | Large. |
| `.-size-sm` | Small. |
| `.-size-small` | Small. Long-form alias of `-size-sm`. |
| `.-toggle` | A pressed-state toggle button (drive with aria-pressed). |
| `.-without-background` | Drop the fill (ghost). |
| `.-without-border` | Remove the border. |

## Pseudo-elements

| Pseudo-element | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `::after` | The AI-secondary gradient border ring, masked to just the button's frame. |
| `::before` | The AI glyph, added automatically to AI buttons and masked in the variant's own colour. |

## States

| State | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `:disabled` | — |
| `:state(pressed)` | — |

<result>Write isn't available in this read-only context, so here's the assessment directly.

# Critical assessment: block-level prose translation for generated API docs

First, two premises to correct up front, because they change the cost math:

- **There are no `Defined in` lines in the current output** (0 of 589 files). That churn source doesn't exist today, so it can't be a justification. The real whole-file churn drivers are: signature edits, cssdoc token *value* changes (the `## Tokens consumed` table in `docs/api/css/button.md:71-148`), and stability-badge flips (`<span class="... pantoken-doc-tag">` — Alpha 97, Beta 481, Experimental 308, Deprecated 27). Badges flip often and sit at the top of nearly every TypeDoc page, so a single stability re-tag currently busts the whole page. That's a genuinely good argument for block-level — but it's the badge/token churn, not line numbers.
- **Block-level does NOT reduce cold-run cost — it increases it, unless you batch.** Distinct prose lines are ~2029 (TypeDoc) + ~550 (css) ≈ 2600, versus 589 whole files. Per-segment `translateMarkdown` would mean ~2600 sequential `claude -p` calls — worse than the whole-file path and a direct violation of the `build-and-docs.md` constraint. The win from block-level is **warm-cache stability**, not cold cost. To also win on cold cost you must **batch prose** (see Q3).

## Q1 — Is the adapter-agnostic cache serving claude prose to a glossary CI build sound?

**The read path is sound; the write path has one real corruption vector.**

Read path: `keyFor(kind, source)` (`translation-memory.ts:32`) omits the adapter, so a claude-populated `prose` entry is served to a glossary run as a plain cache hit (`translateUnits`, `translation-memory.ts:123-127`). This is exactly how the guides already work. Fine.

`save()` pruning is also fine for *retention*: on any run, every segment present in the tree is `get()`-ed (marked used) or `set()` on miss (marked used), so pruning only drops orphans — segments no longer emitted. It never drops claude prose that's still in use. And CI never commits (docs.yml builds + deploys only), so a CI glossary run rewriting hu.api.json in the runner is harmless.

**The corruption vector — poison-cache.** The `glossary` adapter does not translate prose; it only does structural term replacement. If a glossary run hits a **miss** on a `prose` segment (new or edited paragraph), `translateUnits` still calls the adapter, gets back near-English text, and `memory.set(...)` stores it under the prose key (`translation-memory.ts:140` / `162`). If that file is ever committed, a later claude run will `get()` that key, hit the cache, and **never re-translate it** — the English stub is permanently masked from claude until the source text changes. In the whole-file design this is latent but avoided by workflow discipline; at block granularity the surface is every new paragraph, so it will bite.

Mitigation (required, not optional): the pipeline must not persist glossary output for `prose` units. # Add API TypeDoc / cssdoc prose to the i18n workflow

## Context

The docs site (`docs/`, VitePress, locales `root`=EN and `hu`=Hungarian) already has a full i18n
pipeline, and it already runs over the generated API tree — but only with the deterministic
**`glossary`** adapter, which swaps ~55 fixed TypeDoc structural terms and leaves all authored prose
in English. So `docs/hu/api/**` shows Hungarian section scaffolding but English descriptions,
accessibility notes, and modifier tables. Hand-written guides, by contrast, are real Hungarian
(someone ran the `claude-code` adapter once and committed the output + cache).

The gap is deliberate: `docs/conventions/build-and-docs.md` warns "don't run `:claude` over the whole
API tree — a cold cache means hundreds of sequential `claude -p` calls." The generated tree is
also rebuilt from scratch on every `docs:build`, so we can't just commit translated `.md` files the
way guides do — the build regenerates them.

**Goal:** ship real Hungarian prose for the TypeDoc + cssdoc reference, durably, without paying a
per-build claude cost and without breaking the CI constraint (CI has `vp` but not `pnpm`, and must
not make claude calls).

**Why this design.** The translation memory (`docs/i18n-cache/hu.api.json`) is content-addressed and
**adapter-agnostic** — its key is `sha256(kind + " " + source)`, with no record of what produced the
value. So a committed claude-authored entry is served to a *glossary* CI build as an ordinary cache
hit. That's the lever: run claude once locally, commit the cache, and CI's glossary build serves the
prose from cache, falling back to glossary only for genuinely new content. The remaining problem is
**granularity**: whole-file cache keys thrash on generated docs (a stability-badge flip at the top of
almost every TypeDoc page, or a cssdoc token-value change, busts the whole page → its prose reverts
to English under glossary). The fix is to translate at **prose-block** granularity so the cache
survives scaffolding churn, and to **batch** the prose so the one-time cold run stays ~30–40 calls
instead of ~2,600.

## Approach

Segment each generated `.md` into ordered blocks classified as `preserve` (verbatim), `heading`
(deterministic glossary), or `prose` (real translation). Cache and translate only prose blocks,
individually. Batch prose through the adapter so the cold run is affordable. Extend the glossary to
cover the cssdoc headings and stability-badge labels it currently misses. Add a guard so a glossary
run never persists English passthrough under a prose key (poison-cache prevention).

## Changes

### 1. New module — `docs/scripts/segment-markdown.ts`

Pure, unit-tested. Exports `segmentMarkdown(md): Segment[]` and `reassemble(segments, translations):
string`, where `Segment = { kind: "preserve" | "heading" | "prose"; text: string }`.

Classification (blank-line-delimited blocks + a stateful fence scanner — reuse the `inFence` logic in
`api-translation.ts:179-200`):

- **preserve** — frontmatter, fenced code (```` ``` ````, ```` ```demo ````), HTML blocks (badge
  `<span class="…pantoken-doc-tag">`, `<div class="css-example">`), TypeDoc breadcrumbs, signature
  blockquotes (`> **name**(…)`), type lines, link-only lines, identifier headings (`### nextConfig?`).
- **heading** — structural/cssdoc section headings (`## Parameters`, `## Accessibility`, `# CSS: …`).
  Routed through the glossary so they stay deterministic and never enter the cache.
- **prose** — running-text paragraphs (component summaries, section intros, `@remarks`, TypeDoc param
  descriptions — which render as standalone paragraphs, not tables), `@example` captions, and list-item
  trailing prose after an em-dash (e.g. the `Related` bullets in `docs/api/css/button.md:152`).

**Tables (cssdoc Description columns — in scope for v1).** Detect GFM tables; if a table has a
`Description` header column, translate each non-empty description cell (skip `—`) as a prose unit,
protecting inline code within the cell, and preserve every other column and the table structure. This
covers the Modifiers / Pseudo-elements / Related descriptions that hold much of a component page's
authored prose (see `docs/api/css/button.md:34-54`). Tables with no Description column (Tokens
consumed, States-with-only-`—`) are preserved whole. Reassembly reinserts translated cells by position.

### 2. `docs/scripts/api-translation.ts`

- **Extend `SORTED_REPLACEMENTS` (`:20-73`)** with the ~20 cssdoc section headings actually emitted
  (Accessibility, Usage, Demo, Modifiers, Pseudo-elements, States, Tokens consumed, Related, Structure,
  Parts, Slots, Custom properties, Conditions, Animations, Subcomponents, Browser support, See, …;
  source of truth = `cssdoc.jsonc` `render.sectionOrder`) and the stability-badge labels `Alpha`,
  `Beta`, `Experimental` (`Deprecated` is already mapped). Keep the `CSS:` heading prefix mapping too.
- **Add placeholder protection to the batch path (`translateBatch`/`runBatch`, `:258-302`).** Today the
  batch path protects neither inline code nor `@scope/pkg` names; prose cells/paragraphs carry both.
  Wrap each value through `preserveMarkdownSensitiveBlocks` + `preservePackageNames` before building the
  JSON payload and restore after. (The per-file `translateMarkdown` path already does this.)

### 3. `docs/scripts/translation-memory.ts`

- **Widen `TranslationUnit.kind` (`:22`)** to include `"prose"`.
- **Route `prose` misses through the batched path**, not the per-file loop (`:137-151`). At the existing
  6000-char budget this is ~30–40 requests for the whole cold tree, honoring the "no hundreds of calls"
  constraint while giving per-paragraph warm granularity. Keep `autosave` so the run is resumable.
- **Poison-cache guard (required).** When the active adapter is `glossary`, do **not** `memory.set(...)`
  for a `prose` miss — glossary can't translate prose, and persisting its English passthrough under the
  prose key would permanently mask that block from a later claude run. Cleanest signal: have
  `GlossaryTranslationAdapter` advertise that it doesn't handle prose (e.g. a `translatesProse = false`
  flag), and skip the `set()` for prose misses under it. The rendered file still gets the passthrough;
  the cache just stays clean.

### 4. `docs/scripts/build-api-locales.ts`

- **Replace the per-file markdown loop (`:116-129`)** with: read each `.md` → `segmentMarkdown` →
  collect its `prose` segments as units → one `translateUnits` pass (`kind: "prose"`, `autosave: true`)
  over all files' prose → route `heading` segments through the glossary → `reassemble` → write.
  Sidebar handling (`:133-149`) is unchanged.
- **Fold-in fix (`:96`):** switch `run("pnpm", ["exec", "typedoc", …])` to `run("vp", ["exec",
  "typedoc", …])`. CI runs `vp run @pantoken/docs#docs:build` with **no pnpm on PATH**
  (`.github/workflows/docs.yml:41` says so), and that path reaches this line — the current `pnpm exec`
  is a latent deploy break. `build-api-locales` only runs top-level (not from inside VitePress), so
  `vp exec` is safe here (no nested-spawn issue). Verify locally after the switch.

### 5. Cache migration (self-cleaning)

The first block-level run emits only `prose`/`text` units, never `markdown`, so the old whole-file
`markdown` keys are never touched and `save()`'s prune-to-used (`:82-91`) drops them automatically — no
manual step. The first run **must** be `docs:api:locales:claude` (cold), which repopulates
`hu.api.json` with prose; a glossary-first run would leave prose untranslated (guard) rather than
poison the cache. One-time, resumable, ~30–40 calls — acceptable.

### 6. Docs — `docs/conventions/build-and-docs.md`

Rewrite the "Adapter split" bullet (`:47-49`): describe the block-level prose model, the
adapter-agnostic committed cache, and the workflow — run `docs:api:locales:claude` locally to author
prose, commit `hu.api.json`, and CI's glossary `docs:build` serves it from cache (glossary now only
fills structural headings/labels and any brand-new prose falls back to passthrough, never poisons).

## Scripts / workflow

No new package.json scripts needed — `docs:api:locales` (glossary, CI) and `docs:api:locales:claude`
(manual authoring) already exist. The workflow becomes: edit source doc comments → run
`pnpm run docs:api:locales:claude` locally → commit `docs/hu/api` regen is not committed, but
`docs/i18n-cache/hu.api.json` **is** → CI serves prose from that cache.

## Verification

1. **Unit tests** for `segment-markdown.ts`: identity round-trip (`reassemble(segmentMarkdown(x),
   identity) === x`) on real fixtures — a cssdoc page (`docs/api/css/button.md`) and a TypeDoc function
   page (`docs/api/bundlers/next/src/functions/withPantoken.md`); plus classification assertions
   (badges/signatures/tables-without-Description preserved; summaries/param paragraphs/Description cells
   marked prose; section headings marked heading).
2. **Cold claude run:** `pnpm run docs:api:locales:claude`. Confirm the run makes ~30–40 batched calls
   (not hundreds), is resumable, and that `docs/hu/api/css/button.md` now shows Hungarian summary,
   Accessibility prose, Modifiers Description cells, and Hungarian section headings — with code fences,
   token tables, `@scope/pkg` names, and badges intact.
3. **Glossary re-serve (the CI path):** `pnpm run docs:api:locales`. Confirm prose is served from the
   committed cache with **no English regression**, and that a glossary miss on a synthetic new
   paragraph is left as passthrough but **not** written to `hu.api.json` (poison guard).
4. **Parity:** `pnpm run docs:check:locales`.
5. **Full gate:** `pnpm run ready` + `pnpm run check:publish`.
6. **Render check:** build and start a preview on a distinct `--strictPort`, then spot-check a HU
   cssdoc page and a HU TypeDoc page render correctly (headings, tables, live css-example previews).

## Out of scope

- Additional locales beyond `hu` (the machinery is locale-parametrized; no work implied here).
- Making the TypeDoc/cssdoc renderers locale-aware at the source-comment level (we post-process
  rendered markdown, matching the existing pipeline).

  blockquotes (`> **name**(…)`), type lines, link-only lines, identifier headings (`### nextConfig?`).
- **heading** — structural/cssdoc section headings (`## Parameters`, `## Accessibility`, `# CSS: …`).
  Routed through the glossary so they stay deterministic and never enter the cache.
- **prose** — running-text paragraphs (component summaries, section intros, `@remarks`, TypeDoc param
  descriptions — which render as standalone paragraphs, not tables), `@example` captions, and list-item
  trailing prose after an em-dash (e.g. the `Related` bullets in `docs/api/css/button.md:152`).

**Tables (cssdoc Description columns — in scope for v1).** Detect GFM tables; if a table has a
`Description` header column, translate each non-empty description cell (skip `—`) as a prose unit,
protecting inline code within the cell, and preserve every other column and the table structure. This
covers the Modifiers / Pseudo-elements / Related descriptions that hold much of a component page's
authored prose (see `docs/api/css/button.md:34-54`). Tables with no Description column (Tokens
consumed, States-with-only-`—`) are preserved whole. Reassembly reinserts translated cells by position.

- **Extend `SORTED_REPLACEMENTS` (`:20-73`)** with the ~20 cssdoc section headings actually emitted
  (Accessibility, Usage, Demo, Modifiers, Pseudo-elements, States, Tokens consumed, Related, Structure,
  Parts, Slots, Custom properties, Conditions, Animations, Subcomponents, Browser support, See, …;
  source of truth = `cssdoc.jsonc` `render.sectionOrder`) and the stability-badge labels `Alpha`,
  `Beta`, `Experimental` (`Deprecated` is already mapped). Keep the `CSS:` heading prefix mapping too.
- **Add placeholder protection to the batch path (`translateBatch`/`runBatch`, `:258-302`).** Today the
  batch path protects neither inline code nor `@scope/pkg` names; prose cells/paragraphs carry both.
  Wrap each value through `preserveMarkdownSensitiveBlocks` + `preservePackageNames` before building the
  JSON payload and restore after. (The per-file `translateMarkdown` path already does this.)

### 3. `docs/scripts/translation-memory.ts`

- **Widen `TranslationUnit.kind` (`:22`)** to include `"prose"`.
- **Route `prose` misses through the batched path**, not the per-file loop (`:137-151`). At the existing
  6000-char budget this is ~30–40 requests for the whole cold tree, honoring the "no hundreds of calls"
  constraint while giving per-paragraph warm granularity. Keep `autosave` so the run is resumable.
- **Poison-cache guard (required).** When the active adapter is `glossary`, do **not** `memory.set(...)`
  for a `prose` miss — glossary can't translate prose, and persisting its English passthrough under the
  prose key would permanently mask that block from a later claude run. Cleanest signal: have
  `GlossaryTranslationAdapter` advertise that it doesn't handle prose (e.g. a `translatesProse = false`
  flag), and skip the `set()` for prose misses under it. The rendered file still gets the passthrough;
  the cache just stays clean.

### 4. `docs/scripts/build-api-locales.ts`

- **Replace the per-file markdown loop (`:116-129`)** with: read each `.md` → `segmentMarkdown` →
  collect its `prose` segments as units → one `translateUnits` pass (`kind: "prose"`, `autosave: true`)

  `vp exec` is safe here (no nested-spawn issue). Verify locally after the switch.

The first block-level run emits only `prose`/`text` units, never `markdown`, so the old whole-file
`markdown` keys are never touched and `save()`'s prune-to-used (`:82-91`) drops them automatically — no

No new package.json scripts needed — `docs:api:locales` (glossary, CI) and `docs:api:locales:claude`
(manual authoring) already exist. The workflow becomes: edit source doc comments → run
`pnpm run docs:api:locales:claude` locally → commit `docs/hu/api` regen is not committed, but

1. **Unit tests** for `segment-markdown.ts`: identity round-trip (`reassemble(segmentMarkdown(x),

4. **Parity:** `pnpm run docs:check:locales`.
5. **Full gate:** `pnpm run ready` + `pnpm run check:publish`.
6. **Render check:** build and start a preview on a distinct `--strictPort`, then spot-check a HU
   cssdoc page and a HU TypeDoc page render correctly (headings, tables, live css-example previews).

## Out of scope

- Additional locales beyond `hu` (the machinery is locale-parametrized; no work implied here).
- Making the TypeDoc/cssdoc renderers locale-aware at the source-comment level (we post-process
  rendered markdown, matching the existing pipeline).

1	# Add API TypeDoc / cssdoc prose to the i18n workflow
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	The docs site (`docs/`, VitePress, locales `root`=EN and `hu`=Hungarian) already has a full i18n
6	pipeline, and it already runs over the generated API tree — but only with the deterministic
7	**`glossary`** adapter, which swaps ~55 fixed TypeDoc structural terms and leaves all authored prose
8	in English. So `docs/hu/api/**` shows Hungarian section scaffolding but English descriptions,
9	accessibility notes, and modifier tables. Hand-written guides, by contrast, are real Hungarian
10	(someone ran the `claude-code` adapter once and committed the output + cache).
11	
12	The gap is deliberate: `docs/conventions/build-and-docs.md` warns "don't run `:claude` over the whole
13	API tree — a cold cache means hundreds of sequential `claude -p` calls." The generated tree is
14	also rebuilt from scratch on every `docs:build`, so we can't just commit translated `.md` files the
15	way guides do — the build regenerates them.
16	
17	**Goal:** ship real Hungarian prose for the TypeDoc + cssdoc reference, durably, without paying a
18	per-build claude cost and without breaking the CI constraint (CI has `vp` but not `pnpm`, and must
19	not make claude calls).
20	
21	**Why this design.** The translation memory (`docs/i18n-cache/hu.api.json`) is content-addressed and
22	**adapter-agnostic** — its key is `sha256(kind + " " + source)`, with no record of what produced the
23	value. So a committed claude-authored entry is served to a *glossary* CI build as an ordinary cache
24	hit. That's the lever: run claude once locally, commit the cache, and CI's glossary build serves the
25	prose from cache, falling back to glossary only for genuinely new content. The remaining problem is
26	**granularity**: whole-file cache keys thrash on generated docs (a stability-badge flip at the top of
27	almost every TypeDoc page, or a cssdoc token-value change, busts the whole page → its prose reverts
28	to English under glossary). The fix is to translate at **prose-block** granularity so the cache
29	survives scaffolding churn, and to **batch** the prose so the one-time cold run stays ~30–40 calls
30	instead of ~2,600.
31	
32	## Approach
33	
34	Segment each generated `.md` into ordered blocks classified as `preserve` (verbatim), `heading`
35	(deterministic glossary), or `prose` (real translation). Cache and translate only prose blocks,
36	individually. Batch prose through the adapter so the cold run is affordable. Extend the glossary to
37	cover the cssdoc headings and stability-badge labels it currently misses. Add a guard so a glossary
38	run never persists English passthrough under a prose key (poison-cache prevention).
39	
40	## Changes
41	
42	> **Order:** land Change 0 (glossary refresh) first — it's a small, deterministic, CI-safe change
43	> that immediately fixes the live HU site (which is glossary-only today), and it's a prerequisite for
44	> the prose work's `heading` routing. The block-level prose work (Changes 1–6) follows.
45	
46	### 0. Refresh the stale glossary — `docs/scripts/api-translation.ts`
47	
48	The cssdoc doc-block tags (`@accessibility`, `@usage`, `@modifier`, `@part`, …) were added after the
49	glossary was last touched, so their rendered headings, table columns, and badge labels never got
50	entries and render in **English** on the live HU site. Audit of `docs/api/**` vs `SORTED_REPLACEMENTS`
51	(`:20-73`) — all confirmed **missing**:
52	
53	- **Section headings** (add as phrase entries; order multi-word before any single-word component,
54	  e.g. `Custom properties` and `Tokens consumed` before `Properties`/existing entries): Usage,
55	  Tokens consumed, Modifiers, Related, Accessibility, Pseudo-elements, Structure, Parts, States,
56	  Browser support, Demo, Subcomponents, Custom properties, Conditions, Animations, Slots, Extends.
57	- **Stability badge labels**: Alpha, Beta, Experimental (Deprecated is already mapped). These sit in
58	  `<span class="…pantoken-doc-tag">` blocks — glossary-substitute the known label text even though the
59	  span is otherwise preserved (fixed closed set; no HTML goes to claude).
60	- **Table column headers**: Modifier, Pseudo-element, Part, State, Slot, Animation, Token, Query, Name,
61	  Summary, Value. **Do not add the generic ones (Value, Name, Type, Summary, Query) as blanket
62	  `\bWord\b` replacements** — they collide with prose. Translate them **header-row-scoped** inside the
63	  table-aware segmenter (Change 1), so only the table's header cells are mapped, never prose.

68	### 1. New module — `docs/scripts/segment-markdown.ts`
69	
70	Pure, unit-tested. Exports `segmentMarkdown(md): Segment[]` and `reassemble(segments, translations):
71	string`, where `Segment = { kind: "preserve" | "heading" | "prose"; text: string }`.
72	
73	Classification (blank-line-delimited blocks + a stateful fence scanner — reuse the `inFence` logic in
74	`api-translation.ts:179-200`):
75	
76	- **preserve** — frontmatter, fenced code (```` ``` ````, ```` ```demo ````), HTML blocks (badge
77	  `<span class="…pantoken-doc-tag">`, `<div class="css-example">`), TypeDoc breadcrumbs, signature
78	  blockquotes (`> **name**(…)`), type lines, link-only lines, identifier headings (`### nextConfig?`).
79	- **heading** — structural/cssdoc section headings (`## Parameters`, `## Accessibility`, `# CSS: …`).
80	  Routed through the glossary so they stay deterministic and never enter the cache.
81	- **prose** — running-text paragraphs (component summaries, section intros, `@remarks`, TypeDoc param
82	  descriptions — which render as standalone paragraphs, not tables), `@example` captions, and list-item
83	  trailing prose after an em-dash (e.g. the `Related` bullets in `docs/api/css/button.md:152`).
84	
85	**Tables (cssdoc Description columns — in scope for v1).** Detect GFM tables; if a table has a
86	`Description` header column, translate each non-empty description cell (skip `—`) as a prose unit,
87	protecting inline code within the cell, and preserve every other column and the table structure. This
88	covers the Modifiers / Pseudo-elements / Related descriptions that hold much of a component page's
89	authored prose (see `docs/api/css/button.md:34-54`). Tables with no Description column (Tokens
90	consumed, States-with-only-`—`) are preserved whole. Reassembly reinserts translated cells by position.
91	
92	### 2. `docs/scripts/api-translation.ts`
93	
94	- **Glossary entries** — already covered by Change 0 (section headings, badge labels, header-scoped
95	  table columns). The `heading` segments from Change 1 route through this same glossary.
96	- **Add placeholder protection to the batch path (`translateBatch`/`runBatch`, `:258-302`).** Today the
97	  batch path protects neither inline code nor `@scope/pkg` names; prose cells/paragraphs carry both.
98	  Wrap each value through `preserveMarkdownSensitiveBlocks` + `preservePackageNames` before building the
99	  JSON payload and restore after. (The per-file `translateMarkdown` path already does this.)
100	
101	### 3. `docs/scripts/translation-memory.ts`
102	
103	- **Widen `TranslationUnit.kind` (`:22`)** to include `"prose"`.
104	- **Route `prose` misses through the batched path**, not the per-file loop (`:137-151`). At the existing
105	  6000-char budget this is ~30–40 requests for the whole cold tree, honoring the "no hundreds of calls"
106	  constraint while giving per-paragraph warm granularity. Keep `autosave` so the run is resumable.
107	- **Poison-cache guard (required).** When the active adapter is `glossary`, do **not** `memory.set(...)`
108	  for a `prose` miss — glossary can't translate prose, and persisting its English passthrough under the
109	  prose key would permanently mask that block from a later claude run. Cleanest signal: have
110	  `GlossaryTranslationAdapter` advertise that it doesn't handle prose (e.g. a `translatesProse = false`
111	  flag), and skip the `set()` for prose misses under it. The rendered file still gets the passthrough;
112	  the cache just stays clean.
113	
114	### 4. `docs/scripts/build-api-locales.ts`
115	
116	- **Replace the per-file markdown loop (`:116-129`)** with: read each `.md` → `segmentMarkdown` →
117	  collect its `prose` segments as units → one `translateUnits` pass (`kind: "prose"`, `autosave: true`)
118	  over all files' prose → route `heading` segments through the glossary → `reassemble` → write.
119	  Sidebar handling (`:133-149`) is unchanged.
120	- **Fold-in fix (`:96`):** switch `run("pnpm", ["exec", "typedoc", …])` to `run("vp", ["exec",
121	  "typedoc", …])`. CI runs `vp run @pantoken/docs#docs:build` with **no pnpm on PATH**
122	  (`.github/workflows/docs.yml:41` says so), and that path reaches this line — the current `pnpm exec`
123	  is a latent deploy break. `build-api-locales` only runs top-level (not from inside VitePress), so
124	  `vp exec` is safe here (no nested-spawn issue). Verify locally after the switch.
125	
126	### 5. Cache migration (self-cleaning)
127	
128	The first block-level run emits only `prose`/`text` units, never `markdown`, so the old whole-file
129	`markdown` keys are never touched and `save()`'s prune-to-used (`:82-91`) drops them automatically — no
130	manual step. The first run **must** be `docs:api:locales:claude` (cold), which repopulates
131	`hu.api.json` with prose; a glossary-first run would leave prose untranslated (guard) rather than
132	poison the cache. One-time, resumable, ~30–40 calls — acceptable.
133	
134	### 6. Docs — `docs/conventions/build-and-docs.md`
135	
136	Rewrite the "Adapter split" bullet (`:47-49`): describe the block-level prose model, the
137	adapter-agnostic committed cache, and the workflow — run `docs:api:locales:claude` locally to author
138	prose, commit `hu.api.json`, and CI's glossary `docs:build` serves it from cache (glossary now only
139	fills structural headings/labels and any brand-new prose falls back to passthrough, never poisons).
140	
141	## Scripts / workflow
142	
143	No new package.json scripts needed — `docs:api:locales` (glossary, CI) and `docs:api:locales:claude`
144	(manual authoring) already exist. The workflow becomes: edit source doc comments → run
145	`pnpm run docs:api:locales:claude` locally → commit `docs/hu/api` regen is not committed, but
146	`docs/i18n-cache/hu.api.json` **is** → CI serves prose from that cache.
147

151	   the HU headings now localize — grep `docs/hu/api/css/button.md` and a few TypeDoc pages for the
152	   previously-English headings (Usage, Accessibility, Modifiers, Tokens consumed, …) and the badge
153	   labels (Alpha/Beta/Experimental), and confirm no prose word (a stray "value"/"name") got
154	   over-translated. This step is meaningful before any prose work exists.
155	1. **Unit tests** for `segment-markdown.ts`: identity round-trip (`reassemble(segmentMarkdown(x),
156	   identity) === x`) on real fixtures — a cssdoc page (`docs/api/css/button.md`) and a TypeDoc function
157	   page (`docs/api/bundlers/next/src/functions/withPantoken.md`); plus classification assertions

# Add API TypeDoc / cssdoc prose to the i18n workflow

## Context

The docs site (`docs/`, VitePress, locales `root`=EN and `hu`=Hungarian) already has a full i18n
pipeline, and it already runs over the generated API tree — but only with the deterministic
**`glossary`** adapter, which swaps ~55 fixed TypeDoc structural terms and leaves all authored prose
in English. So `docs/hu/api/**` shows Hungarian section scaffolding but English descriptions,
accessibility notes, and modifier tables. Hand-written guides, by contrast, are real Hungarian
(someone ran the `claude-code` adapter once and committed the output + cache).

The gap is deliberate: `docs/conventions/build-and-docs.md` warns "don't run `:claude` over the whole
API tree — a cold cache means hundreds of sequential `claude -p` calls." The generated tree is
also rebuilt from scratch on every `docs:build`, so we can't just commit translated `.md` files the
way guides do — the build regenerates them.

**Goal:** ship real Hungarian prose for the TypeDoc + cssdoc reference, durably, without paying a
per-build claude cost and without breaking the CI constraint (CI has `vp` but not `pnpm`, and must
not make claude calls).

**Why this design.** The translation memory (`docs/i18n-cache/hu.api.json`) is content-addressed and
**adapter-agnostic** — its key is `sha256(kind + " " + source)`, with no record of what produced the
value. So a committed claude-authored entry is served to a *glossary* CI build as an ordinary cache
hit. That's the lever: run claude once locally, commit the cache, and CI's glossary build serves the
prose from cache, falling back to glossary only for genuinely new content. The remaining problem is
**granularity**: whole-file cache keys thrash on generated docs (a stability-badge flip at the top of
almost every TypeDoc page, or a cssdoc token-value change, busts the whole page → its prose reverts
to English under glossary). The fix is to translate at **prose-block** granularity so the cache
survives scaffolding churn, and to **batch** the prose so the one-time cold run stays ~30–40 calls
instead of ~2,600.

## Approach

Segment each generated `.md` into ordered blocks classified as `preserve` (verbatim), `heading`
(deterministic glossary), or `prose` (real translation). Cache and translate only prose blocks,
individually. Batch prose through the adapter so the cold run is affordable. Extend the glossary to
cover the cssdoc headings and stability-badge labels it currently misses. Add a guard so a glossary
run never persists English passthrough under a prose key (poison-cache prevention).

## Changes

> **Order:** land Change 0 (glossary refresh) first — it's a small, deterministic, CI-safe change
> that immediately fixes the live HU site (which is glossary-only today), and it's a prerequisite for
> the prose work's `heading` routing. The block-level prose work (Changes 1–6) follows.

### 0. Refresh the stale glossary — `docs/scripts/api-translation.ts`

The cssdoc doc-block tags (`@accessibility`, `@usage`, `@modifier`, `@part`, …) were added after the
glossary was last touched, so their rendered headings, table columns, and badge labels never got
entries and render in **English** on the live HU site. Audit of `docs/api/**` vs `SORTED_REPLACEMENTS`
(`:20-73`) — all confirmed **missing**:

- **Section headings** (add as phrase entries; order multi-word before any single-word component,
  e.g. `Custom properties` and `Tokens consumed` before `Properties`/existing entries): Usage,
  Tokens consumed, Modifiers, Related, Accessibility, Pseudo-elements, Structure, Parts, States,
  Browser support, Demo, Subcomponents, Custom properties, Conditions, Animations, Slots, Extends.
- **Stability badge labels**: Alpha, Beta, Experimental (Deprecated is already mapped). These sit in
  `<span class="…pantoken-doc-tag">` blocks — glossary-substitute the known label text even though the
  span is otherwise preserved (fixed closed set; no HTML goes to claude).
- **Table column headers**: Modifier, Pseudo-element, Part, State, Slot, Animation, Token, Query, Name,
  Summary, Value. **Do not add the generic ones (Value, Name, Type, Summary, Query) as blanket
  `\bWord\b` replacements** — they collide with prose. Translate them **header-row-scoped** inside the
  table-aware segmenter (Change 1), so only the table's header cells are mapped, never prose.

Author Hungarian consistent with the existing entries. This change alone can ship and be verified
against a glossary rebuild before any prose work begins.

### 1. New module — `docs/scripts/segment-markdown.ts`

Pure, unit-tested. Exports `segmentMarkdown(md): Segment[]` and `reassemble(segments, translations):
string`, where `Segment = { kind: "preserve" | "heading" | "prose"; text: string }`.

Classification (blank-line-delimited blocks + a stateful fence scanner — reuse the `inFence` logic in
`api-translation.ts:179-200`):

- **preserve** — frontmatter, fenced code (```` ``` ````, ```` ```demo ````), HTML blocks (badge
  `<span class="…pantoken-doc-tag">`, `<div class="css-example">`), TypeDoc breadcrumbs, signature
  blockquotes (`> **name**(…)`), type lines, link-only lines, identifier headings (`### nextConfig?`).
- **heading** — structural/cssdoc section headings (`## Parameters`, `## Accessibility`, `# CSS: …`).
  Routed through the glossary so they stay deterministic and never enter the cache.
- **prose** — running-text paragraphs (component summaries, section intros, `@remarks`, TypeDoc param
  descriptions — which render as standalone paragraphs, not tables), `@example` captions, and list-item
  trailing prose after an em-dash (e.g. the `Related` bullets in `docs/api/css/button.md:152`).

**Tables (cssdoc Description columns — in scope for v1).** Detect GFM tables; if a table has a
`Description` header column, translate each non-empty description cell (skip `—`) as a prose unit,
protecting inline code within the cell, and preserve every other column and the table structure. This
covers the Modifiers / Pseudo-elements / Related descriptions that hold much of a component page's
authored prose (see `docs/api/css/button.md:34-54`). Tables with no Description column (Tokens
consumed, States-with-only-`—`) are preserved whole. Reassembly reinserts translated cells by position.

### 2. `docs/scripts/api-translation.ts`

- **Glossary entries** — already covered by Change 0 (section headings, badge labels, header-scoped
  table columns). The `heading` segments from Change 1 route through this same glossary.
- **Add placeholder protection to the batch path (`translateBatch`/`runBatch`, `:258-302`).** Today the
  batch path protects neither inline code nor `@scope/pkg` names; prose cells/paragraphs carry both.
  Wrap each value through `preserveMarkdownSensitiveBlocks` + `preservePackageNames` before building the
  JSON payload and restore after. (The per-file `translateMarkdown` path already does this.)

### 3. `docs/scripts/translation-memory.ts`

- **Widen `TranslationUnit.kind` (`:22`)** to include `"prose"`.
- **Route `prose` misses through the batched path**, not the per-file loop (`:137-151`). At the existing
  6000-char budget this is ~30–40 requests for the whole cold tree, honoring the "no hundreds of calls"
  constraint while giving per-paragraph warm granularity. Keep `autosave` so the run is resumable.
- **Poison-cache guard (required).** When the active adapter is `glossary`, do **not** `memory.set(...)`
  for a `prose` miss — glossary can't translate prose, and persisting its English passthrough under the
  prose key would permanently mask that block from a later claude run. Cleanest signal: have
  `GlossaryTranslationAdapter` advertise that it doesn't handle prose (e.g. a `translatesProse = false`
  flag), and skip the `set()` for prose misses under it. The rendered file still gets the passthrough;
  the cache just stays clean.

### 4. `docs/scripts/build-api-locales.ts`

- **Replace the per-file markdown loop (`:116-129`)** with: read each `.md` → `segmentMarkdown` →
  collect its `prose` segments as units → one `translateUnits` pass (`kind: "prose"`, `autosave: true`)
  over all files' prose → route `heading` segments through the glossary → `reassemble` → write.
  Sidebar handling (`:133-149`) is unchanged.
- **Fold-in fix (`:96`):** switch `run("pnpm", ["exec", "typedoc", …])` to `run("vp", ["exec",
  "typedoc", …])`. CI runs `vp run @pantoken/docs#docs:build` with **no pnpm on PATH**
  (`.github/workflows/docs.yml:41` says so), and that path reaches this line — the current `pnpm exec`
  is a latent deploy break. `build-api-locales` only runs top-level (not from inside VitePress), so
  `vp exec` is safe here (no nested-spawn issue). Verify locally after the switch.

### 5. Cache migration (self-cleaning)

The first block-level run emits only `prose`/`text` units, never `markdown`, so the old whole-file
`markdown` keys are never touched and `save()`'s prune-to-used (`:82-91`) drops them automatically — no
manual step. The first run **must** be `docs:api:locales:claude` (cold), which repopulates
`hu.api.json` with prose; a glossary-first run would leave prose untranslated (guard) rather than
poison the cache. One-time, resumable, ~30–40 calls — acceptable.

### 6. Docs — `docs/conventions/build-and-docs.md`

Rewrite the "Adapter split" bullet (`:47-49`): describe the block-level prose model, the
adapter-agnostic committed cache, and the workflow — run `docs:api:locales:claude` locally to author
prose, commit `hu.api.json`, and CI's glossary `docs:build` serves it from cache (glossary now only
fills structural headings/labels and any brand-new prose falls back to passthrough, never poisons).

## Scripts / workflow

No new package.json scripts needed — `docs:api:locales` (glossary, CI) and `docs:api:locales:claude`
(manual authoring) already exist. The workflow becomes: edit source doc comments → run
`pnpm run docs:api:locales:claude` locally → commit `docs/hu/api` regen is not committed, but
`docs/i18n-cache/hu.api.json` **is** → CI serves prose from that cache.

## Verification

   the HU headings now localize — grep `docs/hu/api/css/button.md` and a few TypeDoc pages for the
   previously-English headings (Usage, Accessibility, Modifiers, Tokens consumed, …) and the badge
   labels (Alpha/Beta/Experimental), and confirm no prose word (a stray "value"/"name") got
   over-translated. This step is meaningful before any prose work exists.
1. **Unit tests** for `segment-markdown.ts`: identity round-trip (`reassemble(segmentMarkdown(x),
   identity) === x`) on real fixtures — a cssdoc page (`docs/api/css/button.md`) and a TypeDoc function
   page (`docs/api/bundlers/next/src/functions/withPantoken.md`); plus classification assertions
   (badges/signatures/tables-without-Description preserved; summaries/param paragraphs/Description cells
   marked prose; section headings marked heading).
2. **Cold claude run:** `pnpm run docs:api:locales:claude`. Confirm the run makes ~30–40 batched calls
   (not hundreds), is resumable, and that `docs/hu/api/css/button.md` now shows Hungarian summary,
   Accessibility prose, Modifiers Description cells, and Hungarian section headings — with code fences,
   token tables, `@scope/pkg` names, and badges intact.
3. **Glossary re-serve (the CI path):** `pnpm run docs:api:locales`. Confirm prose is served from the
   committed cache with **no English regression**, and that a glossary miss on a synthetic new
   paragraph is left as passthrough but **not** written to `hu.api.json` (poison guard).
4. **Parity:** `pnpm run docs:check:locales`.
5. **Full gate:** `pnpm run ready` + `pnpm run check:publish`.
6. **Render check:** build and start a preview on a distinct `--strictPort`, then spot-check a HU
   cssdoc page and a HU TypeDoc page render correctly (headings, tables, live css-example previews).

## Out of scope

- Additional locales beyond `hu` (the machinery is locale-parametrized; no work implied here).
- Making the TypeDoc/cssdoc renderers locale-aware at the source-comment level (we post-process

# Build, release, and the docs site

## Use the `vp` toolchain, never pnpm directly

- `vp` / `vpr` / `vpx` are **global** bins. Run tasks via `vp run <task>`, execute bins via `vp exec
[-F <glob>] <bin>`.
- **Package scripts must never shell out to `pnpm`.** CI (`.github/workflows/docs.yml`) provides `vp`
  via `voidzero-dev/setup-vp` but **not** `pnpm` on PATH, so a `pnpm run …` inside any script breaks
  the docs deploy with `pnpm: command not found`. Local dev has pnpm, so a top-level `pnpm run X` is
  fine — but scripts it calls must stay pnpm-free internally.
- `.css` formatting: `vp fmt` (oxc) is JS/TS/JSON only and no-ops on `.css`. Stylelint owns `.css` —
  `lint:css` runs `stylelint --fix`, wired into `ready` and the `vite.config.ts` `staged` hook.

## The gate

- `pnpm run ready` — build `-r`, `vp check`, test `-r`, markdown lint. Must pass before you're done.
- `pnpm run check:publish` — `publint`.
- Release automation uses Changesets and package-tag workflows in
  `.github/workflows/release.yml`.
- Use `pnpm run release:version` to apply package changelog/version updates, then
  `vp run release:changelog:root` to rebuild the strict chronological root `CHANGELOG.md` before
  creating package tags.
- Generated artifacts are gitignored and reproduced on build: `platforms/tokens/src/generated/`,
  `platforms/css/style.css`, each preprocessor's static file, and web-components `src/generated/`.
  `ready` runs `vp run -r build` before `vp check`, so generated files exist in order.

See `docs/internal/release-strategy.md` for the runbook, dist-tag mapping, prerelease flow, and npm
organization governance model.

## Linting CSS

Root `stylelint.config.js` runs error-only core rules plus `@cssdoc/stylelint-plugin`'s
`cssdoc/valid-doc-comments`; anchor-positioning props are ignored and `@scope` is allowed. A parallel
`eslint.config.js` runs `@cssdoc/eslint-plugin` (via `@eslint/css`) over the same `.css` (`lint:js`).
`lint:css` targets the web-components `src/**/*.css` sources and the generated components CSS.

## The docs site

`docs/` is a VitePress site (`@pantoken/docs`) with two locales — `root` (English, `/…`) and `hu`
(Magyar, `/hu/…`) — a symmetric prefix swap that VitePress's default routing already handles (don't
set a custom `i18nRouting`).

- **Translation layer is `docs/.vitepress/i18n.ts`.** `LOCALES[locale]` holds every localizable UI
  string (nav/sidebar labels, `editText`, the theme selector, VitePress chrome labels, and local
  search). `config.ts` expands these into per-locale `themeConfig` (search is the exception — it lives
  in the global `themeConfig.search.options.locales`). Add new UI strings here, never inline.
- **Adapter split.** Hand-written guides use the `claude-code` adapter; the generated API tree
  (TypeDoc + CSS reference) uses the deterministic `glossary` adapter. Don't run `:claude` over the
  whole API tree — a cold cache means hundreds of sequential `claude -p` calls.

## The cssdoc integration

pantoken consumes `@cssdoc/*` from **npm** (catalog entries; consumers use `catalog:`), not a local
workspace link. `docs/scripts/build-css-api.ts` is a thin wrapper: it builds pantoken's `resolveToken`
(syntax + value + local vars) and `resolveDemo` hooks, then calls `@cssdoc/typedoc`'s `emitCssApi`,
and keeps the `unknownReferences` drift guard. All page/index/sidebar rendering lives in
`@cssdoc/markdown`. The live `<div class="css-example">` preview is pantoken's own
`@pantoken/typedoc-plugin-live-example`, kept out of `@cssdoc/markdown` so the upstream stays generic.

**Catalog gotcha:** cssdoc packages reference `catalog:` deps; if cssdoc adds a new one, pantoken's
catalog must carry it too, or install fails with `ERR_PNPM_CATALOG_ENTRY_NOT_FOUND_FOR_SPEC`.

## The nested-`vp`-spawn limitation

Under `vpr docs:dev`, VitePress runs _under_ `vp`. Any `vp run …` / `vp pack` spawned from **inside**
that process dies with `Failed to spawn process: Invalid argument (os error 22)` on a cache miss. A
direct `node scripts/x.ts` is unaffected. So:

- The docs orchestrator's `upstream[].build` uses `["node","scripts/generate.ts"]` (cwd = the package
  dir), not a nested `vp run`.
- The CSS-API node runs `["node","scripts/build-css-api.ts"]` (cwd `docs`).
- `@pantoken/web-components`' `register()` bundle genuinely needs `vp pack` (which also can't nest), so
  it's not in the live orchestrator — rebuild it in a separate top-level shell
  (`vpr @pantoken/web-components#build`); `reloadWatchPaths` on its `dist` bridges the change into HMR.

A `vp run X && vp run Y` chain _inside_ a package.json script is fine — that's a top-level
script-runner context, not a spawn from within the running VitePress process.

# CSS: button

`.instui-button` — An accessible action control, styled from the token palette; primary by default.

The AI variants layer two gradients — a padding-box fill and a border-box stroke — for their frame, and `-color-ai-secondary` can't paint gradient text and a fill at once, so its centre stays transparent at rest and fills on hover or active. Ghost hover and active derive a low-opacity, slightly-darkened brand wash rather than using the raw hover-background tokens, which would print same-colour-on-same-colour text.

**Source:** [button.ts](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/blob/main/formats/components/src/components/button.ts)

## Akadálymentesség

Drive the `-toggle` variant's pressed state with `aria-pressed`, and mark a disabled button with `aria-disabled` (or the native `disabled`).

## Módosítók

| `.-color-primary-inverse` | Primary action for dark backgrounds. |

# CSS: button

`.instui-button` – Akadálymentes műveleti vezérlő, a tokenpaletta alapján stílusozva; alapértelmezés szerint elsődleges.

Az MI-változatok a kerethez két színátmenetet rétegeznek egymásra – egy padding-box kitöltést és egy border-box körvonalat –, és mivel az `-color-ai-secondary` nem tud egyszerre színátmenetes szöveget és kitöltést festeni, a közepe alaphelyzetben átlátszó marad, és csak hover vagy aktív állapotban telik meg. A ghost hover és aktív állapot alacsony áttetszőségű, kissé sötétített márkarétegből származik, nem a nyers hover-background tokenekből, amelyek azonos színű szöveget nyomtatnának azonos színre.

**Forrás:** [button.ts](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/blob/main/formats/components/src/components/button.ts)

## Akadálymentesség

Az `-toggle` változat lenyomott állapotát az `aria-pressed` vezérli, letiltott gombot pedig az `aria-disabled` (vagy a natív `disabled`) jelöl.

## Használat

```css
@import "@pantoken/components/components.css";
@import "@pantoken/components/button.css";
```

## Demó

```demo
self:button
```

## Példák

```html
<button class="instui-button">Primary</button>
```

## Módosítók

| Módosító | Leírás |
| --- | --- |
| `.-color-ai` | MI-művelet. |
| `.-color-ai-secondary` | Kisebb hangsúlyú MI-művelet. |
| `.-color-danger` | Destruktív művelet. |
| `.-color-primary-inverse` | Elsődleges művelet sötét háttérhez. |
| `.-color-secondary` | Kisebb hangsúlyú másodlagos művelet. |
| `.-color-success` | Megerősítő/pozitív művelet. |
| `.-color-tertiary` | Szöveg stílusú művelet (hoverig se kitöltés, se keret). |
| `.-condensed` | Szűkebb belső margó sűrű eszköztárakhoz. |
| `.-display-block` | Teljes szélességű blokkgomb. |
| `.-ghost` | Körvonalas (ghost) stílus: keret a szín ghost tokenjeivel, kitöltés nélkül. |
| `.-icon-*` | Az ikonkészletből egy glyph megjelenítése a címke előtt (pl. `-icon-arrow-right`), a gomb szövegszínével festve; párosítsd az `-shape-square`/`-shape-circle` tulajdonsággal, ha csak ikonból álló gombot szeretnél. |
| `.-shape-circle` | Kerek ikongomb. |
| `.-shape-square` | Négyzet alakú ikongomb. |
| `.-size-large` | Nagy. Az `-size-lg` hosszú alakú aliasa. |
| `.-size-lg` | Nagy. |
| `.-size-sm` | Kicsi. |
| `.-size-small` | Kicsi. Az `-size-sm` hosszú alakú aliasa. |
| `.-toggle` | Lenyomott állapotú kapcsológomb (az aria-pressed vezérli). |
| `.-without-background` | Kitöltés elhagyása (ghost). |
| `.-without-border` | A keret eltávolítása. |

## Pszeudoelemek

| Pszeudoelem | Leírás |
| --- | --- |
| `::after` | Az MI-másodlagos színátmenetes keretgyűrű, a gomb keretére maszkolva. |
| `::before` | Az MI glyph, automatikusan hozzáadva az MI-gombokhoz, és a változat saját színére maszkolva. |

## Állapotok

| Állapot | Leírás |
| --- | --- |
| `:disabled` | — |
| `:state(pressed)` | — |

# CSS: button

`.instui-button` – Akadálymentes műveleti vezérlő, a tokenpaletta alapján stílusozva; alapértelmezés szerint elsődleges.

Az MI-változatok a kerethez két színátmenetet rétegeznek egymásra – egy padding-box kitöltést és egy border-box körvonalat –, és mivel az `-color-ai-secondary` nem tud egyszerre színátmenetes szöveget és kitöltést festeni, a közepe alaphelyzetben átlátszó marad, és csak hover vagy aktív állapotban telik meg. A ghost hover és aktív állapot alacsony áttetszőségű, kissé sötétített márkarétegből származik, nem a nyers hover-background tokenekből, amelyek azonos színű szöveget nyomtatnának azonos színre.

**Forrás:** [button.ts](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/blob/main/formats/components/src/components/button.ts)

## Akadálymentesség

Az `-toggle` változat lenyomott állapotát az `aria-pressed` vezérli, letiltott gombot pedig az `aria-disabled` (vagy a natív `disabled`) jelöl.

```css
@import "@pantoken/components/components.css";

```

```demo
self:button
```
